artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma = \{0,1\}$ be the binary alphabet, and let $\Sigma^*$ denote the set of finite words over $\Sigma$. Two words $u, v \in \Sigma^*$ are said to be abelian equivalent, written $u \sim_a v$, if $|u| = |v|$ and, for every letter $a \in \Sigma$, the number of occurrences of $a$ in $u$ equals the number of occurrences of $a$ in $v$. An abelian cube is a nonempty word of the form $u_1 u_2 u_3$ with $u_1, u_2, u_3 \in \Sigma^+$ and $u_1 \sim_a u_2 \sim_a u_3$; the common length $|u_1| = |u_2| = |u_3|$ is called the (abelian) period of the cube. A (finite or infinite) word $w$ is said to avoid abelian cubes of period at least $k$ if no factor of $w$ is an abelian cube of period $\geq k$.

Question: Does there exist a positive integer $k$ such that there is an infinite word over $\Sigma = \{0,1\}$ avoiding all abelian cubes of period at least $k$?
artifact.status_search_result: Rao and Rosenfeld (in "Avoidability of long k-abelian repetitions", arXiv:1507.02581, 2015, published in Mathematics of Computation, 2016) proved that one cannot avoid abelian cubes of abelian period at least 2 in infinite binary words. This answers the question in the negative: no such integer $k$ exists.

status_evidence.title: Avoidability of long k-abelian repetitions
status_evidence.snippet: One cannot avoid abelian-cubes of abelian period at least 2 in infinite binary words, therefore answering negatively a question from Mäkelä.
status_evidence.claim: Rao and Rosenfeld proved that abelian cubes of period at least k cannot be avoided over a binary alphabet for any k ≥ 2, settling the question negatively.

status_evidence.title: Avoidability of long k-abelian repetitions (Math. Comp.)
status_evidence.snippet: Published version showing that one cannot avoid abelian cubes of abelian period at least 2 over a binary alphabet.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms the negative resolution of Mäkelä's question on avoiding long abelian cubes over binary alphabets.
